name: CWF Anarchy Championship
notes: Source: the SeVeN show script, which headers the match "CWF Anarchy Championship — Anarchy Rules" and ring-announces Mr. X the winner (promotions/cwf/archive/seven-2003-02-01.html); the Redz()ne-2 card, which bills Mr. X "(Champ)" defending against Sean Manning in a Dumpster Match (promotions/cwf/archive/redzone-2-card-2003-03-11.html). No dedicated title-history page for this belt survives.
epitaph: Crowned in a three-way at SeVeN — reduced to a two-way mid-match when Starter was written out by an in-story lightning strike — and won by Mr. X, who pinned Hardcore Z with his own legs on the ropes. The Redz()ne-2 card bills him defending it against Sean Manning in a Dumpster Match ten days later; that show's own results were never captured, so the belt's own history ends there, mid-defense, in the surviving record.

name: CWF World Championship
notes: Source: the SeVeN show script, headered "CWF World Championship — Normal Rules," whose own commentary calls the winner "our first heavyweight champion since 2001" (promotions/cwf/archive/seven-2003-02-01.html). No dedicated title-history page for this belt survives.
epitaph: Billed the fed's own first heavyweight champion since 2001, the belt changed hands once in the surviving record: 'The Natural' Mike Diamond outlasted Paco at SeVeN, submitting him to the Midas Touch with a compromised special guest referee counting the fall, then was immediately confronted by a returning, unmasked Kid Gangster, who produced a signed contract forcing a title match against owner Hellfire X. Whether that match was ever wrestled is not attested anywhere in the surviving record.

name: Cold Championship
notes: Source: the Redz()ne-2 card, which bills two "Cold Championship Tournament" quarter-finals — Chain against Starter, and Paco against Ice (promotions/cwf/archive/redzone-2-card-2003-03-11.html). No results page for this card survives.
epitaph: A tournament title never crowned in the surviving record. Redz()ne-2's own card bills two Cold Championship Tournament quarter-finals — Chain against Starter, Paco against Ice — but the show's own results were never captured, so no holder, semi-final or final is attested anywhere in the held record.
